fallback_endpoints.description: Replicas of the same provider, tried after `endpoint`. A call moves on only when its request never left, or (read-only capabilities) when its response was lost or the endpoint answered 502, 503 or 504; three consecutive failures eject an endpoint for 30 seconds, doubling up to five minutes. Each must serve the same tools and share the provider's state; OAuth tokens name `endpoint` as their resource unless `oauth.resource` is set.

id.description: Adapter id that capability manifests name.

oauth.description: Obtain provider tokens with the OAuth client credentials grant instead of a fixed token (see `runtime::oauth_broker`).

result_projection.description: MCP only: how a tool result becomes the tool output. `flat` (the default) is the original mapping; `mcp_result_v1` preserves structured content losslessly.

token_env.description: Environment variable holding the provider credential issued by your broker.

AmountThreshold.description: An amount at or above which approvals need step-up, in one currency.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, as the action's bound `amount.currency`.

agent_ids.description: The agent ids this key is issued for (see `agent_binding`).

scopes.description: API scopes granted, such as `admit`, `dispatch` or `audit:read`.

key_id.description: Key id (`kid`) recorded on every entry the current key signs.

kms.description: Sign with a key held in a KMS instead (the runtime then never holds it).

retired_keys.description: Public keys of retired signing keys. Entries they signed stay verifiable after a rotation: verifiers trust them, and `GET /v1/audit/keys` publishes them, but nothing signs with them.

signing_seed_env.description: Environment variable holding the 32-byte ed25519 seed as hex (development, or a secret store that only hands out seeds). Unused when `kms` is set.

id.description: Sink id, used in metrics and delivery cursors.

kinds.description: Entry kinds to deliver; every kind when empty.

mask.description: Payload fields to mask (see the module documentation).

mask_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the masking key (at least 32 bytes); required with `mask`.

secret_env.description: Environment variable holding the request signing secret (at least 32 bytes).

start.description: `genesis` (default): deliver each tenant's whole chain; `head`: from now on.

oneOf.description: ASCII letters compared without case (`ORD_881` is `ord_881`).

CompletionScores.description: `[guards] completion_requires_scores`: on or off, or explicit floors.

ConformanceConfig.description: Principals whose conformance reports and control evidence this deployment trusts, with the Ed25519 keys their attestations are signed with (see `attest`). Each principal names its tenant; an assessment uses those of the caller's tenant only. The caller of an assessment never supplies these.

trusted_assessors.description: Principals whose conformance reports are trusted.

trusted_evidence_observers.description: Principals whose control evidence is trusted.

DelegationConfig.description: `[oidc.delegation]`: how a delegated token names its actor and user.

actor_agent_claim.description: Field of the actor object naming the agent, mapped through the issuer's `agents` table (Keycloak: `client_id`). Unset: the issuer's `agent_claim`.

actor_claim.description: Claim path of the actor object (its `sub` is the caller).

user_roles_claim.description: Claim path listing the user's roles (Keycloak: `realm_access.roles`). Set, a run may declare only a role the user holds.

EvidenceIssuerConfig.description: `[[evidence_issuers]]`: one service trusted to vouch for named facts.

jwks.description: Its public keys as a JWK Set (JSON text, as the issuer publishes it). A `kid` in an attestation's header selects one; several keys allow rotation.

max_validity_seconds.description: The longest `valid_until - observed_at` it may claim.

tenants.description: Tenants whose runs may rely on it.

from.description: JSON Pointer into `{"request": …, "run_context": …}` to a string or number.

prefix.description: Prepended to the run's value to form the expected `sub`.

agent_binding.description: Whether a run's declared agent must be one its caller's credential is issued for (`required`, `observe`, `off`; see `agent_binding`). Unset: `required` with the `contextos.enterprise` profile, `observe` otherwise.

approval_step_up.description: Approvals above an amount, or of named capabilities, count only after the approver's recent strong sign-in (see `contextos_gateway::step_up`).

completion_requires_scores.description: Online validation: a run may complete only when every decision that applied an effect holds an independent score whose `policy` and `safety` meet these floors. Unset: on in production (policy 1.0, safety 0.9), off in development; `true` uses those floors, `false` opts out explicitly, a table sets them.

evidence.description: What may satisfy a decision's evidence gate (`strict`, `caller`; see `evidence_admission`). Unset: `strict` with the `contextos.enterprise` profile, which requires it, `caller` otherwise.

identical_tool_calls.description: Identical tool calls (same capability and arguments, new operation) a run may make before the next is refused with `loop_detected`; 0 disables the guard.

model_call_min_tokens.description: Tokens every model-call reservation covers at least, so an executor cannot reserve (and self-settle) a model call for nothing.

pack_intents.description: Whether a run's intent must be one its Context Pack's rules name (`required`, `observe`, `off`; see `pack_intents`). Unset: `required` with the `contextos.enterprise` profile, `observe` otherwise.

refuse_repeated_effects.description: Refuse a new operation whose effect is identical (same capability and arguments) to one the run already applied, unless the capability is `repeatable`: `effect_repeated`. On by default.

require_completion_contracts.description: Refuse to start with an effectful MCP capability that declares no `recovery.completion`, so a finished result is confirmed by the state the tool reports, not by the absence of `isError`. Unset: on in production, off in development. (Effectful HTTP capabilities always need one.)

require_task_authorization.description: Refuse runs that can apply effects unless they state what their principal authorized (`task_authorization`), so no effect relies on the agent's own reading of the request.

require_tool_schemas.description: Refuse to start with a capability that lacks an `input_schema` or `output_schema`, so every call's arguments and results are checked against a reviewed shape (read-only tools too: their results carry most injected content).

require_user_role.description: Refuse runs whose user claims carry no `role`, so policy never evaluates a role nobody asserted (the reference compiler defaults it; see the threat model). Unset: on in production, off in development.

required_release_refs.description: Release artifact types every run's execution contract must pin in `release_refs` (e.g. `["model_profile", "evaluator_suite"]`), so each decision records which model and evaluators produced it. Unset: `model_profile` and `evaluator_suite` in production, none in development; `[]` opts out explicitly.

trust_supplied_memory.description: Admit recalled memory (`deps.promoted_memory`) that no memory-governance service can verify. Without `[providers.memory]`, production refuses such memory unless this is set; with it, every item is verified against promoted state regardless.

user_binding.description: Whether a run's declared user must be the user its caller's delegated token acts for (`required`, `observe`, `off`; see `user_binding`). Unset: `observe`.

gateway_principal_id.description: Principal id the gateway uses for its own observations.

trust_domain.description: Trust domain of agent principals admitted by this deployment.

key_version.description: The Transit key version that signs (pinned: a rotation inside Vault does not silently change what this `key_id` means).

public_key.description: The expected Ed25519 public key (base64url, unpadded) of that version. Startup fails if the KMS reports another, so a hijacked endpoint cannot substitute its own.

token_env.description: Environment variable holding the Vault token.

heartbeat_ms.description: How often replicas record their heartbeat for shared tenant limits.

max_concurrent_dispatch.description: Default per-tenant governed effects in progress at once.

max_in_flight.description: Requests in progress across all tenants; beyond it the server answers 503.

requests_per_second.description: Default per-tenant request rate (token bucket refill), shared across replicas.

oneOf.description: Enables development-only conveniences; never use with real tenants.

OAuthClientConfig.description: OAuth 2.0 client credentials for one adapter's provider.

client_secret_env.description: Environment variable holding the client secret.

refresh_before_seconds.description: Replace a cached token this long before it expires.

resource.description: RFC 8707 resource the token is for; defaults to the adapter's endpoint.

scope.description: Scope to request, if the server needs one.

token_url.description: Token endpoint of the authorization server.

agent_claim.description: Claim naming the agent the token is issued for (for example `sub` of a SPIFFE JWT-SVID, or `azp`), checked against the run's declared agent at admission.

agents.description: Maps an `agent_claim` value to the agent ids it may run as. Empty: the claim value itself is the agent id.

delegation.description: Accept RFC 8693 delegated tokens: the caller is the actor, acting for a user.

jwks_url.description: HTTPS URL of the issuer's JWKS (HTTP is allowed only in development mode). Unset: discovered from the issuer's OpenID Provider Metadata.

refresh_seconds.description: How often the JWKS is fetched again.

scope_claim.description: Space-separated string or array of scopes.

tenant_claim.description: Claim path naming the tenant: a string, an array or an object keyed by name (Keycloak's `organization`). It must name exactly one of `tenants`.

tenant_map.description: Maps `tenant_claim` values (for example Keycloak organization aliases) to tenant ids. Empty: the claim value itself is the tenant id.

tenants.description: Tenants this issuer may assert. A token naming any other tenant is rejected.

approvals.description: Approvals service: human approval requests and decisions.

authority.description: Authority service: who may act for whom.

boundary.description: Execution-boundary controller; when set, run start, resume and every dispatch require the kernel to find the run's boundary active.

constraints.description: Constraints service: verified observations for the controls a pack requires.

data_flow.description: Data-governance service; when set, data sent to destinations must pass the kernel's data-flow policy evaluation.

idempotency.description: Provider idempotency status service, for reconciling unknown outcomes.

memory.description: Memory-governance service; enables governed memory lifecycle operations.

resource_identity.description: Resource identity service; maps identifiers to canonical ids for guarantees with `resource_canonicalizer = "provider"`.

result_screening.description: Result-screening service; judges every confirmed effect's output before the agent sees it.

timeout_ms.description: Time a call may take before it counts as failed.

token_env.description: Environment variable holding this service's bearer credential.

ResourceCanonicalizer.description: How a guarantee makes a resource identifier canonical before keying its ledger.

path.description: JSON Schema file the result must meet.

batch.description: Runs erased per sweep at most.

run_content_days.description: Erase a run's personal content this many days after admission; unset keeps it.

sweep_interval_ms.description: How often the erasure sweep runs.

kid.description: The retired key's id, as recorded on the entries it signed.

public_key.description: Base64url (unpadded) of the 32-byte Ed25519 public key, as `GET /v1/audit/keys` published it.

retired_at.description: When the key stopped signing: it verifies only entries emitted up to then, so a retired key that later leaks cannot sign new history.

allowed_origins.description: Browser origins, besides `public_url`'s, that may call the MCP endpoint.

listen.description: Socket address to listen on, such as `0.0.0.0:8080`.

max_body_bytes.description: Largest request body accepted, in bytes.

mode.description: `production` refuses development-only conveniences and warns about weak settings.

public_url.description: The URL clients reach this server at, for OAuth protected resource metadata (see `protected_resource`). Unset: no metadata is published.

request_timeout_ms.description: Time a request may take before the server answers 504.

tls.description: Serve HTTPS (and require client certificates, with `client_ca_path`) without a terminating proxy (see `tls_server`). Unset: plain HTTP behind your proxy.

amount_pointer.description: JSON pointer to the amount in the call's arguments, such as `/amount_minor`.

capability_ids.description: Capabilities whose effects draw on this limit.

id.description: Guarantee id, recorded on every reservation.

limit.description: Total amount all runs together may commit per resource.

owner_after_seconds.description: How old a hold is before its owner is told (default 1,800 seconds).

owner_route.description: The notification webhook that tells this guarantee's business owner about a hold older than `owner_after_seconds` (see `hold_owners`). Routing only: not part of the pinned definition.

resource_canonicalizer.description: How the extracted identifier is made canonical (see `resource_identity`); omitted from the definition when `exact`.

resource_pointer.description: JSON pointer to the resource identifier in the call's arguments, such as `/order_id`.

unit.description: Unit of `limit` and the amounts, such as `INR_minor`.

amount_at_least.description: Applies to actions whose bound amount reaches the threshold for its currency, and to any bound amount in a currency without one (or without a currency).

amr_values.description: Accepted `amr` methods (any one present), for example `mfa`, `hwk`, `otp`.

capabilities.description: Applies to every approval of these capabilities.

max_age_seconds.description: How long before the decision the approver may have authenticated.

url_env.description: Environment variable holding the connection URL.

controls.description: Controls this deployment actually enforces through its integrated providers. Declaring a control here is a claim about the deployment, not a grant.

implementation_id.description: Implementation id published in the support declaration.

implementation_version.description: Implementation version published in the support declaration.

burst.description: This tenant's bucket size; unset uses the default.

max_concurrent_dispatch.description: This tenant's concurrent effects; unset uses the default.

requests_per_second.description: This tenant's request rate; unset uses the default.

tenant_id.description: The tenant these limits apply to.

cert_path.description: PEM file with the server certificate, then its intermediates.

client_ca_path.description: PEM file of the CAs that issue client certificates. Set: every client must present one (mutual TLS). Unset: clients are not asked for a certificate.

header_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a connection may sit with no request in progress, and an HTTP/1.1 client may take to send a request's headers, before it is closed (at least 1).

key_path.description: PEM file with the server's private key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1).

max_connections.description: Most connections open at once (at least 1); further clients wait to be accepted.

reload_secs.description: How often to check the files for a rotated certificate; 0 never reloads.

TrustedSigner.description: A trusted principal and the Ed25519 key its attestations are signed with.

principal.description: The signer's principal, including its tenant.

public_key.description: Base64 (standard) of the 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

id.description: Webhook id, which guarantees name in `owner_route` and metrics label.

link_template.description: Link to the decision, with `{escalation_id}`, `{run_id}` and `{tenant_id}` replaced (for example your Tower URL).

max_attempts.description: Attempts per event before it is given up (logged and counted).

secret_env.description: Environment variable holding the signing secret (at least 32 bytes).

adapters.description: Providers that perform effects: MCP servers or HTTP services.

api_keys.description: API keys, configured as hashes only (`ctx hash-key`).

audit_sinks.description: Destinations the audit chain is delivered to, with masked payload fields (see `audit_sinks`).

capabilities.description: Reviewed capability manifest JSON files to pin at startup.

evidence_issuers.description: Services trusted to vouch for gated evidence (see `evidence_issuers`).

evidence_subjects.description: What each gated requirement's evidence must be about (see `evidence_subjects`).

guarantees.description: Trusted business-resource limits shared by unrelated agent runs.

identity.description: Agent trust domain and the gateway's own principal; defaults suit one deployment.

notifications.description: Webhooks told when escalations open and resolve (see `notifications`).

oidc.description: OIDC issuers whose JWTs authenticate callers.

pack_dirs.description: Directories whose JSON files (recursively; names starting with `.` skipped) are Context Packs, loaded at startup and re-read on reload (see `pack_registry`).

pack_reload_secs.description: Re-read `packs` and `pack_dirs` this often and add new pack versions; 0 (the default) reads them at startup and on `POST /v1/packs/reload` only.

packs.description: Context Pack JSON files to load at startup.

providers.description: Remote fact services; dispatch is disabled without them.

result_schemas.description: Schemas delegated runs' results must meet, by the `output_schema_ref` a delegation names: `[[result_schemas]] ref = "schema://…", path = "…json"`.

retention.description: Retention of runs' personal content (see `retention`); off by default.

retired_capabilities.description: Manifests of versions `capabilities` replaced, kept while operations claimed under them may still need reconciliation or attestation. Never dispatched.

server.description: The listener, request limits and mode.

store.description: Where runs, ledgers and the audit chain are kept.

support.description: What this deployment declares it implements (`RuntimeSupportDeclaration`).
